title: capacity-skyline-onboarding-scenarios-sheet
body:
Purpose:
Outline probabilistic capacity impact for onboarding a new medium-size 13B model family across regions. This is a working sheet — high-level numbers for design and discussion. Not a final runbook.

Summary (TL;DR):
- New model X (13B, multi-head KV footprint profile) expected to increase per-request KV residency by ~80MiB on average when active.
- Baseline traffic mix: 60% short queries (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512).
- Three scenarios modeled: Optimistic (low adoption), Baseline (projected adoption ramp), Conservative (fast adoption + burst).
- Key output: projected GPU headroom per region and recommended admission safety buffer (concurrency headroom) to keep 99.9th latency SLOs during first 30 days.

Assumptions and notes (explicit):
- Model variant: 13B fp16 (quantized path available but not default until day 14).
- KV object average size: 480 bytes; active prefix mean sequence length 1536 tokens -> mean KV per request = 80MiB (includes overhead).
- Average token generation rate: 20 tokens/sec per request when streaming.
- Average GPU slot (T4-equivalent normalized) can support 6 concurrent short requests, 3 medium, 1 long, without KV cache thrashing.
- Cross-region affinity coefficient: US-West 0.6, US-East 0.25, EU 0.1, APAC 0.05 (fraction of requests originating there).
- Warmup behavior: first 24h shows a 2.8x cold-start penalty on GPU utilization due to cache misses and KV rehydration.
- Eviction churn tax: estimated 12% additional GPU cycles lost to KV eviction overhead when cache occupancy > 85%.

Scenario definitions:
- Optimistic: 5% of baseline traffic shifts to the new model over 30d, adoption concentrated in US-West. Quantile tail multipliers low.
- Baseline: 18% shift over 30d, global rollout by day 14, moderate bursts tied to marketing PRs.
- Conservative: 40% shift in first 14 days, early enterprise customers + canary expansion, multi-region bursts and synthetic load tests.

Region inventory (current fleet snapshot):
- US-West: 120 GPUs (G), total KV cache budget assigned: 6TiB, current occupancy: 58%
- US-East: 80 G, KV budget: 4TiB, current occupancy: 62%
- EU: 60 G, KV budget: 3TiB, current occupancy: 49%
- APAC: 32 G, KV budget: 1.5TiB, current occupancy: 44%

Projected per-region delta (first 30 days) formula notes (do in sheet):
- Added KV consumption = active_concurrent_sessions * avg_kv_per_request * priming_factor
- active_concurrent_sessions estimated from traffic shift * baseline_concurrency_per_region / avg_slot_density
- priming_factor: accounts for cold starts and rehydration; assume 2.2 for first 72h, decays to 1.05 by day 14 if warmup seeding used.

Quick worked example (US-West, Baseline scenario):
- Baseline concurrent sessions (all models): 9,600 (derived from 120 GPUs * average slot density 80 sessions per GPU mixed-weight).
- Projected X adoption at day 14: 18% -> 1,728 concurrent X sessions.
- avg_kv_per_request = 80MiB -> projected raw KV demand = 1,728 * 80MiB = 138,240 MiB (~135GiB).
- Priming factor day 1 = 2.2 -> day1 effective KV delta = 297GiB.
- US-West KV headroom (free): 6TiB * (1 - 0.58) = 2.52TiB (~2,580GiB).
- Eviction churn tax at >85% occupancy not hit in this baseline but track for conservative.

Aggregated 30-day projections (summary table, rounded):
- Optimistic total added GPU concurrency equivalent: ~18 GPUs across fleet; KV consumption: +0.9TiB globally.
- Baseline total added GPU concurrency equivalent: ~56 GPUs; KV consumption: +3.2TiB globally.
- Conservative total added GPU concurrency equivalent: ~140 GPUs; KV consumption: +7.1TiB globally (eviction churn likely).

Safety buffer recommendations (derived):
- Optimistic: 15% concurrency safety buffer per-region. No forced rollout guardrails needed.
- Baseline: 25% safety buffer; require staged canary (start 10% -> 30% -> global) and 72h priming seed traffic per region.
- Conservative: 40% safety buffer; require reserved burst capacity (hot standby GPUs) equivalent to 60 GPUs, hard admission control limiting new-user concurrency, and cross-region fallback routes enabled.

Operational mitigations and playbook items:
1) Warmup seeding: 48–72h synthetic priming per region. Use replayed traffic from historical short queries bucket at ~0.5x baseline qps to prepopulate KV.
2) Adaptive admission: start with conservative concurrency thresholds and allow dynamic increase if trace-level SLO checks are green for 1h.
3) Hot-standby pool: allocate spare GPUs in US-West and US-East for first 14 days to absorb initial spikes (recommended: US-West 32 G, US-East 16 G).
4) Fast quantize path: enable quantized variant behind feature flag for enterprise tenants after day 7 to halve per-request KV pressure.
5) Eviction watch: add a 24/7 alert when any region KV occupancy > 80% or eviction rate > 200 evictions/min.
6) Canary metrics: instrument per-model 99.9th latency tail, KV miss ratio, eviction churn, and cross-region redirect ratios.

Open questions / decision points (to discuss):
- Should we reserve dedicated KV shards for enterprise customers of model X to isolate eviction risk? Pros: predictable performance; Cons: wasted capacity if adoption is low.
- Priming budget: who owns the cost of warmup synthetic traffic? Product or infra?
- When to flip quantized-by-default for this model across hosted API? Day 7 pivot vs. day 14 conservative timeline.

Immediate action items (owner tags):
- Run high-fidelity simulation: Marcus Patel -> JIRA JIRA-INF-2156 (due 2026-02-22)
- Prepare warmup job configs (region-specific): Ellen Zhou -> github.com/redwood-inference/infra/ops/warmup-jobs (draft) (due 2026-02-18)
- Set up canary dashboard with 99.9th tail and eviction counts: Ravi Singh -> Confluence and Grafana (due 2026-02-20)

Notes to self:
- This sheet intentionally uses conservative per-request KV estimate; instrument telemetry ASAP to replace assumptions with measured distributions.
- Check overlap with "priming" experiments in infra/experiments folder; avoid double-costing warmup traffic.
- Keep communications short for GTM: provide "safe rollout" checklist the product team can follow.

Appendix (quick formulas):
- avg_kv_delta_gib = concurrent_sessions * avg_kv_mb / 1024 / priming_factor_adjustment
- needed_GPU_equiv = ceil(additional_qps / avg_qps_per_gpu_slot) (account for mixed weight using weighting coefficients)

End of sheet.

(If this looks reasonable we can convert to a spreadsheet with per-day rows for day0..day30, per-region columns, and an automated safety-flag column.)
